text:
Priya: Heads-up — Candidate for Platform Eng moved to 4:00pm today. Need someone to cover system-design panel and take notes. @Elena are you still available?
Elena: I’m free until 4:30, can do first half of the panel.
Priya: Thanks — can you cover the design + scribe first 20m? Then we’ll need a handover for the coding slot.
Samir: I can jump in for the coding portion at 4:20. Happy to be the scoring lead for coding.
Jordan: Quick Q: who owns final pass at normalizing scores? We had a tie last round and need tiebreak rules clarified.
Maya: I can be debrief scribe if Samir takes coding. For tiebreaks, we usually have the hiring manager break ties unless panel votes are split 2:1, then we take average + manager note. Do we want to formalize that? :thinking_face:
Priya: Yes — let’s make it explicit in the debrief form. New plan:
- Scribe: Maya (captures notes + highlights)
- Scoring lead: Samir (finalizes coding numbers)
- Hiring manager break-tie if panel not unanimous
Elena: Fine by me. Also FYI candidate asked about interview length — please keep to schedule.
Priya: Copy. I’m pasting a compact debrief template you can use on the call so notes are consistent.
Priya: ```
Candidate: <name>
Role: Platform Eng
Panel: Elena, Samir, Jordan
Time: 4:00-5:00
Scores (1-5): System design | Coding | Communication
Notes: bullet points per section
Decision: Hire / No hire / Consider with follow-up
Tie-break rationale: note who broke tie + justification
```
Jordan: Love it. Can we add weightings so scoring is explicit? I suggest System design 40%, Coding 40%, Communication 20%.
Samir: Agreed. That helps clarify borderline cases.
Priya: Done — weightings set. I’ll add a quick comment in the calendar invite and ping Interview Bot to attach the template.
Interview Bot: Calendar updated — "Platform Eng interview (4:00pm)". Debrief template attached: https://company.docs/debriefs/templ-2026
Maya: I’ll open the doc at start and drop notes live. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Priya: Appreciate the quick swaps everyone. I’ll signal when handover should happen (4:20).
